_: Option descriptions for the MAUDE Choices beyond the FDA vocabulary. `aliases` maps an openFDA label string to the term FDA's annex now names it (editorial renames), so the option takes that term's official definition and place in the hierarchy. `glosses` is the `what` of the options the annex does not define (R1 and later). R2 overlays, per option, `not_for` and one example: `not_for` names the option's confusable neighbours that are options of the same product code, each as `short[term] (term)`; the neighbours are its parent and children in the annex hierarchy and its siblings when they share a level-2 parent (a top-level category groups problems as unlike as a battery fault and loss of capture), plus `also_not_for`, the few terms the gloss slice shows filed for the same narratives across the hierarchy. `example` is one sentence written from a gloss-slice report filed with that term. `harm` does the same for the event-type Choice. The phrases and examples were written from the gloss slice; which confusions to target was read from the dev rounds, and the manufacturer conventions behind them were cross-checked against pool-wide term counts that include the test reports (issue #10).

aliases.Appropriate Device Problem Term/Code Not: Appropriate Device Problem Term/Code not Available
aliases.Labelling, Instructions for Use or Train: Labeling, Instructions for Use or Training Problem

glosses.Adverse Event Without Identified Device: The patient had an adverse event, such as an infection, a complication or a symptom, and no problem with the device or with how it was used has been identified
glosses.some other problem: A device problem that none of the other options names

short.Activation Problem: a sensor or device that fails to start or activate
short.Activation, Positioning or Separation Pr: a general problem activating, positioning or separating the device
short.Adverse Event Without Identified Device: a patient complication such as capsular contracture, infection or seroma with no device problem identified, as in reports that say it was reported that a patient developed capsular contracture
short.Application Program Freezes or Fails to: an app that freezes, will not open or shows a display issue on a mobile application
short.Appropriate Device Problem Term/Code Not: a device problem no other term fits
short.Biocompatibility: a local or systemic reaction to the device's materials or leachates
short.Break: a component broken or cracked, such as a broken sensor wire or a shell torn while being introduced
short.Capturing Problem: pacing pulses that do not capture the heart
short.Communication or Transmission Problem: a general data transmission problem that is not wireless signal loss
short.Connection Problem: a physical connection between parts that fails, such as a lead that will not fit the header port
short.Decreased Sensitivity: sensing less sensitive than intended, such as low R-wave amplitudes
short.Defective Alarm: an alert that did not work, reported as no alert/notification or an alert/notification settings issue
short.Defibrillation/Stimulation Problem: a general problem with shock or stimulation therapy
short.Device Alarm System: an alarm problem reported in general, such as low glucose alarms that did not sound
short.Device Appears to Trigger Rejection: the body reacting to the implant without a device failure, as in reports where a healthcare professional reported capsular contracture
short.Device Contamination with Chemical or Ot: a chemical or foreign material found on or in the device
short.Device Dislodged or Dislocated: a lead or device that came out of place, such as a lead dislodged after implant
short.Device Displays Incorrect Message: a wrong message or error shown on screen
short.Device Handling Problem: the device mishandled by the user or surgeon
short.Difficult to Open or Remove Packaging Ma: packaging that is hard to open
short.Display or Visual Feedback Problem: a display issue, or glucose values not updating on screen
short.Electromagnetic Interference: noise from an outside electrical source
short.Failure to Convert Rhythm: shocks that did not convert the arrhythmia
short.Failure to Deliver Shock/Stimulation: therapy withheld or delayed when it was needed
short.Failure to Interrogate: a device that could not be interrogated
short.Failure to Power Up: a device that will not power on
short.False Alarm: an alarm with no real condition behind it
short.Fracture: a fractured lead conductor or coil
short.Gel Leak: gel bleeding or leaking from the implant
short.High Capture Threshold: a high or rising pacing threshold
short.High Readings: readings higher than the true glucose value
short.High impedance: impedance measured too high or out of range above
short.Impedance Problem: an impedance change or alert that does not say too high or too low
short.Improper or Incorrect Procedure or Metho: an incorrect surgical or use procedure
short.Inappropriate/Inadequate Shock/Stimulati: a shock or therapy delivered inappropriately, or with the wrong energy or timing
short.Incorrect, Inadequate or Imprecise Resul: erroneous results that are not reported as too high or too low, such as erroneous glucose results against a meter
short.Insufficient Device Problem Information: an event with too little information to name the device problem
short.Interrogation Problem: trouble communicating with the implant by programmer, telemetry or remote monitor
short.Loss of or Failure to Bond: a bond or seal between parts that failed
short.Low Audible Alarm: an alarm too quiet to hear
short.Low Readings: readings lower than the true glucose value, or an inaccuracy between the CGM and a blood glucose meter
short.Malposition of Device: an implant placed or sitting in the wrong position
short.Material Integrity Problem: a general material failure, such as a lead suspected to be broken during implant
short.Material Invagination: a shell folded in on itself
short.Mechanical Problem: a mechanical fault, such as a lead that will not advance into the connector port
short.Migration: an implant that moved from where it was placed
short.No Audible Alarm: an alarm that made no sound
short.No Device Output: no output at all, such as a transmitter battery issue
short.Noise, Audible: an audible noise from the device
short.Nonstandard Device: a device not made to specification
short.Over-Sensing: signals sensed that are not intended beats, such as T-wave oversensing
short.Pacing Problem: pacing delivered incorrectly, such as inappropriate atrial pacing
short.Patient Device Interaction Problem: a general problem between the patient and the device
short.Patient-Device Incompatibility: a device not suited to the patient's anatomy or physiology
short.Premature Discharge of Battery: a battery depleting faster than expected
short.Premature Elective Replacement Indicator: an elective replacement indicator (ERI) reached too early
short.Premature End-of-Life Indicator: an early end of life, or an early sensor expiration
short.Protective Measures Problem: an expected safety alert that never came because of how the system was designed, such as a sensor failure the app does not detect
short.Signal Artifact/Noise: noise or artifact on the sensed signal
short.Under-Sensing: real beats the device failed to sense
short.Unexpected Shutdown: a device or receiver that shut down unexpectedly
short.Unstable Impedance: impedance varying without a clear direction
short.Use of Device Problem: a problem with how the device was used, such as therapy left disabled
short.Wireless Communication Problem: signal loss, or no connection between the sensor or transmitter and the app or receiver

Activation Problem.example: Six sensors in a row failed at start-up.

Adverse Event Without Identified Device.example: It was reported that a patient with Mentor MemoryGel breast implants developed capsular contracture after surgery, and Mentor has no information about explantation.

Application Program Freezes or Fails to.example: It was reported that a display issue occurred on a mobile application.

also_not_for: Adverse Event Without Identified Device or Use Problem
Appropriate Device Problem Term/Code Not.example: The ICD triggered an alert whose cadence indicated a right ventricular lead issue, and the lead remains in use.

Battery Problem.example: The device was explanted due to battery depletion.

also_not_for: Adverse Event Without Identified Device or Use Problem

Break.example: A healthcare professional reported a rupture when introducing the implant; it was not implanted and surgery was completed with a backup device.

Capturing Problem.example: Two days after implant the right ventricular lead showed a rising threshold and intermittent capture.

Connection Problem.example: The right ventricular lead could not fit into the RV port of the device header.

Decreased Sensitivity.example: The right ventricular lead exhibited decreased R-wave amplitudes.

Defective Alarm.example: It was reported that no alert/notification occurred, and the data confirmed that no alert/notification was given.

Detachment of Device or Device Component.example: It was reported that a detached or missing sensor wire occurred.

Device Alarm System.example: An alarm issue was reported: the low glucose alarms did not sound and the customer was not alerted of changes in glucose level.

also_not_for: Adverse Event Without Identified Device or Use Problem
Device Appears to Trigger Rejection.example: A healthcare professional reported capsular contracture Baker grade III on the left side; the device was explanted and replaced.

Device Dislodged or Dislocated.example: The right ventricular lead dislodged after pocket closure on the day of implant and was repositioned.

Device Sensing Problem.example: Atrial tachycardia/atrial fibrillation episodes with non-physiologic ventricular intervals were noted on stored episodes.

Display or Visual Feedback Problem.example: It was reported that a display issue occurred, and glucose values not updating was found in the data.

Electromagnetic Interference.example: Episodes of oversensing were attributed to 60 Hz noise from an outside source.

Failure to Capture.example: The right ventricular lead exhibited an intermittent loss of capture.

Failure to Convert Rhythm.example: The S-ICD needed three shocks to convert the ventricular arrhythmia.

Failure to Deliver Shock/Stimulation.example: The ICD initially withheld therapy for ventricular fibrillation that was detected as supraventricular tachycardia.

Failure to Interrogate.example: The device could not be interrogated.

Failure to Read Input Signal.example: An S-ICD patient received an inappropriate shock due to T-wave oversensing and changes in amplitude morphology measurements.

Fracture.example: The right ventricular lead had a possible fracture and was later replaced.

Gel Leak.example: A patient with Mentor MemoryGel implants had gel bleed on the left side, confirmed during a physical exam.

High Capture Threshold.example: The right ventricular lead exhibited high thresholds and remains in use.

High Readings.example: A high readings issue was reported: the customer received high sensor scan results.

High impedance.example: The ICD recorded high out-of-range shock impedance measurements.

Impedance Problem.example: The right ventricular lead triggered an alert for impedance and remains in use.

Inappropriate or Unexpected Reset.example: The complaint states that a receiver reinitialization was reported.

Inappropriate/Inadequate Shock/Stimulati.example: The ICD delivered inappropriate therapy on atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response that met the ventricular fibrillation detection criteria.

Incorrect, Inadequate or Imprecise Resul.example: A customer reported receiving erroneous glucose results, sensor scan results of 76 mg/dL against 200 mg/dL on a meter.

also_not_for: Appropriate Device Problem Term/Code Not Available
Insufficient Device Problem Information.example: It was reported that a right ventricular lead had an unspecified failure, and no further details could be obtained.

Interrogation Problem.example: During the implant procedure the telemetry connection with the device was lost and could not be re-established.

Low Readings.example: It was reported that an inaccuracy between the continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and the blood glucose (BG) meter occurred, with values in the D zone of the Parkes error grid.

Low impedance.example: The right ventricular lead exhibited low pacing impedance.

Malposition of Device.example: A healthcare professional reported device migration/implant malposition through the National Breast Implant Registry; the device was explanted.

Material Integrity Problem.example: During the implant procedure the physician suspected the lead could be broken, and a new lead was implanted.

Material Rupture.example: A patient with a 400cc Mentor MemoryGel breast implant had a rupture on the right side diagnosed by imaging and is to undergo explantation.

Mechanical Problem.example: During an ICD changeout the chronic lead could not be advanced into the pace/sense port of the new ICD.

Migration.example: After a revision procedure the patient suffered displacement of both breast prostheses.

No Apparent Adverse Event.example: A healthcare professional reported a rupture of the left implant diagnosed by mammogram; the device remains implanted.

No Audible Alarm.example: It was reported that an alert/notification settings issue occurred, and the receiver's speaker and vibrator were tested.

No Device Output.example: It was reported that a transmitter battery issue occurred after the transmitter was started past its use-by date.

Over-Sensing.example: The right ventricular lead exhibited T-wave oversensing and remains in use.

Pacing Problem.example: The ICD performed atrial blanking, which resulted in inappropriate atrial pacing.

Premature Discharge of Battery.example: Data analysis confirmed the battery was depleting more quickly than expected, and device replacement was recommended.

Premature Elective Replacement Indicator.example: The device shows ERI with unexpected battery behavior and remains implanted.

Premature End-of-Life Indicator.example: It was reported that an early sensor expiration occurred.

Protective Measures Problem.example: The user had a sensor failure but did not receive the expected sensor failure alert, because the app only detects that the session has ended.

Signal Artifact/Noise.example: During the implant procedure the right ventricular lead exhibited noise on two analyzers and was replaced.

Under-Sensing.example: The right ventricular lead exhibited one undersensed beat and remains in use.

Unexpected Shutdown.example: It was reported that an unexpected receiver shutdown occurred.

Unintended Application Program Shut Down.example: It was reported that a Dexcom app crash occurred.

Unintended Ejection.example: It was reported that the sensor deployed on its own.

Unstable Impedance.example: A lead integrity alert triggered on the right ventricular lead because of pacing impedance variation.

Use of Device Problem.example: The S-ICD system had therapy disabled for over six months.

Wireless Communication Problem.example: It was reported that signal loss occurred, and signal loss over an hour was found within the investigation window.

Death.not_for: a report where the patient survived (Injury or Malfunction)
Death.example: The lead showed oversensing and loss of capture that appeared to result in asystole, and it was further reported that the patient passed away.

Injury.not_for: a device problem where the device stays in use and the patient needed no treatment (Malfunction)
Injury.example: The right ventricular lead triggered an alert due to noise, a fracture was suspected, and the lead was capped and replaced; no patient complications were reported.

Malfunction.not_for: a report where the device or a lead was explanted, replaced, capped, repositioned or revised, the patient received a shock, or the patient needed treatment or someone else's help, which is a serious injury even when no complication is reported (Injury)
Malfunction.example: The ICD recorded high out-of-range shock impedance measurements; the alert threshold was raised and the ICD remains in service with no adverse patient effects.
